children: Ducati riders could get a new owner as Volkswagen (VWAGY) considers selling the celebrated Italian motorcycle brand.
Ducati is among 600 of Volkswagen's 2,000 businesses under review. Audi CEO Gernot Dollner confirmed that Ducati would be discussed but emphasized that nothing has been decided.
Volkswagen's board approved plans to reduce its businesses and holdings by roughly one-third. A sale could raise cash and simplify the automaker.
Ducati sells about 50,000 motorcycles annually. Ducati generated 925 million in revenue and 52 million in operating profit last year, a 5.6% operating margin.

Bloomberg Intelligence estimates the brand could command approximately 1.25 billion based on peer valuations. Audi acquired Ducati in 2012 and explored selling it in 2017, but dropped the plan after opposition from German labor representatives.
What a Ducati Sale Could Mean for Riders

Nothing changes immediately for owners because this is an evaluation, not a sale. Existing motorcycles, warranties, dealerships and service arrangements remain with Volkswagen unless a transaction advances.

The longer-term implications would depend heavily on the buyer. A well-capitalized owner could increase spending on new models, electrification, dealerships and international expansion. A financially aggressive buyer might instead prioritize higher prices, cost reductions or cash generation.

Ducati's racing program is another crucial consideration. The company has won six consecutive MotoGP constructors' championships since 2020, success that strengthens its engineering credibility and premium brand identity. Any reduction in racing investment could concern enthusiasts, while continued backing could preserve that momentum.

Prospective buyers should therefore avoid treating the review as evidence that Ducati motorcycles or support are suddenly at risk. The practical signals to watch are whether Volkswagen formally hires advisers, identifies bidders or discusses potential terms.

For Volkswagen investors, a sale would matter if the proceeds strengthen its balance sheet or fund higher-priority automotive investments. For riders, the buyer's strategy would matter more than the sale price itself.

title: Volkswagen Considers Move That Could Reshape Ducati
